title: Senate Democrats Introduce Bill to Bar Presidents From Owning Banks, Following World Liberty Financial Charter Approval
dek: The Senate Banking Committee's Democratic minority introduced the Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act on August 15, 2026, in response to the OCC's approval of World Liberty Financial's national bank charter application. The bill would prohibit Presidents, Vice Presidents, their immediate families, and senior government officials from owning or controlling banks. The measure represents legislative pushback against what Democrats characterize as an unprecedented conflict of interest.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Following approval of World Liberty Financial's bank charter application, Senate Banking Committee Democrats led by Elizabeth Warren introduced legislation to bar Presidents and their immediate families from owning or controlling banks.
bottom_line: The bill's introduction marks the opening of a legislative front against Trump administration crypto policy, but its passage prospects depend on Republican Senate cooperation, which the announcement does not address. Watch for the bill's formal assignment of a number, statements from the administration or OCC, and any industry response to the conflict-of-interest framing.
body: The Senate Banking Committee's Democratic minority introduced legislation on August 15, 2026, aimed at preventing sitting Presidents and their families from owning or controlling banks. The Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act was introduced following the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency's approval of World Liberty Financial's national bank charter application on January 5, 2026, according to the Senate Banking Committee.

The bill represents a direct legislative response to what Democratic senators characterize as an unprecedented conflict of interest. According to Senator Elizabeth Warren, the Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, President Trump is now the first President in history to approve, operate, and supervise his own bank. The measure was introduced by Warren alongside Senators Chris Van Hollen, Angela Alsobrooks, Chris Murphy, Bernie Sanders, Richard Blumenthal, Jack Reed, Andy Kim, Tammy Duckworth, and Ruben Gallego, per the Senate Banking Committee announcement.

The bill would establish a blanket prohibition: no President, Vice President, their immediate families, or other senior government officials may exploit their positions to own or control a bank. According to Senator Richard Blumenthal's statement in the announcement, President Trump has systematically weakened oversight of the crypto industry while his family has raked in billions through their numerous crypto schemes, and Trump's hand-picked regulators at the Treasury Department have granted World Liberty Financial a banking charter.

The Democrats' legislative action follows Warren's earlier warnings to Congress on the need to address conflicts of interest. According to the Senate Banking Committee, Warren has been sounding the alarm on this issue since the GENIUS Act passed into law in July 2025. President Trump previously asserted control of the OCC through Executive Order 14215, per the Democrats' characterization in the announcement.

No statement from the Trump administration, the OCC, or World Liberty Financial responding to the bill's introduction is included in the Senate Banking Committee's announcement. The source text does not specify the bill's procedural pathway, likelihood of passage in a Republican-controlled Senate, or when it might receive a floor vote. The scope of terms like immediate families and senior government officials is not defined in the available source material.
